inspection_summary: Inspected all 3,124 normalized lines. The source develops three complexity regimes for computing zeta on the critical line, with the main contribution reducing Riemann-Siegel blocks to small-coefficient cubic exponential sums and then evaluating those sums by an adaptive chain of Poisson/van der Corput transformations, Euler-Maclaurin boundary handling, saddle-point extraction, and parameter-aware FFT precomputation. The text layer is coherent, but exact formulas remain typeset-representation dependent.

sections_inspected.label: Front matter and abstract
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: States the three algorithms and their complexity exponents.

sections_inspected.label: 1. Introduction
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Defines the computational target, compares prior methods, states the main complexity theorem, and motivates repeated normalized Poisson transformations.

sections_inspected.label: 2. Outline of fast methods
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Reduces Riemann-Siegel blocks to polynomial-phase sums and derives the 2/5, 1/3, and 4/13 cost regimes from evaluation and precomputation capabilities.

sections_inspected.label: 3. Idea of the cubic-sum algorithm
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Explains the van der Corput iteration, the cubic self-similarity obstruction, small-coefficient repair, stopping cases, and the implemented two-phase route.

sections_inspected.label: 4. Algorithm setup
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Fixes the computational model and disposes of direct, quadratic, and precomputed boundary regimes.

sections_inspected.label: 4.1 First phase
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Decouples cubic and quadratic components by parity descent until the cubic integral reaches a controlled transition scale.

sections_inspected.label: 4.2 Second phase
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Applies normalized quadratic descent, handles stopping cases, and reduces remainders to controlled integral families.

sections_inspected.label: 4.3 Saddle-point calculations
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Extracts per-term stationary contributions and compresses analytic tails into finite polynomial-phase sums.

sections_inspected.label: 4.4 FFT precomputation
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Builds dyadic grids and a dependency-aware parameterization whose precomputation meets the claimed cost.

sections_inspected.label: 5. Auxiliary results
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Supplies Euler-Maclaurin, derivative, contour, stationary-phase, and quadratic-reduction lemmas needed to certify the algorithm.

accepted_units.title: Single-value zeta computation with exponent 4/13
accepted_units.why_material: States the target accuracy, arithmetic and storage model, precomputation allowance, bit-size control, and independence from the precise Riemann-Siegel remainder.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the computational motivation and complete statement of Theorem 1.1.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The prose is recoverable; exact asymptotic exponents and bounds depend on the displayed formulas.

accepted_units.title: From prior zeta algorithms to normalized Poisson descent
accepted_units.why_material: Relates Euler-Maclaurin, Riemann-Siegel, Schoenhage, and Heath-Brown approaches to the reusable goal of shortening polynomial-phase sums, and explains why normalization between Poisson steps prevents trivial cycling.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the historical baselines and the paper's stated implementation philosophy.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Quoted quadratic approximation and exponential-sum forms are formula-dependent but legible.

accepted_units.title: Block size controls phase degree and global complexity
accepted_units.why_material: Shows how Taylor expansion on common Riemann-Siegel blocks converts logarithmic phases into quadratic, cubic, or higher polynomial phases; the block exponent simultaneously determines phase degree, coefficient scale, and number of blocks.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the general beta-to-degree rule, error truncation, and extension from a prototypical half-sum to the full main sum.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Strongly dependent on equations (2.1)-(2.7) and Tables 1-2; prose makes their structural content recoverable.

accepted_units.title: Lattice overlap and cost balancing in quadratic sums
accepted_units.why_material: Explains Taylor recovery from a coefficient lattice, how overlap among block queries creates reuse, and why balancing lattice precomputation against block count yields the 3/8 FFT and 2/5 direct regimes while motivating a polylogarithmic quadratic-sum algorithm.
accepted_units.context_note: Theorem 2.1 closes the section by supplying the needed pointwise quadratic evaluator.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Lattice coordinates and cost powers require the displayed equations.

accepted_units.title: Small-cubic-coefficient evaluator and its precomputation budget
accepted_units.why_material: Theorem 2.2 isolates the exact cubic coefficient range, pointwise polylogarithmic evaluation cost, and K^(4 mu) precomputation that drive the main zeta algorithm; the following discussion identifies coefficient-range growth and phase degree as the barriers to faster methods.
accepted_units.context_note: Read with the definition of H and the explanation of the mu restriction.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Exact coefficient interval, error, and resource bounds are display-dependent.

accepted_units.title: Riemann-Siegel main sum to bounded polynomial-phase queries
accepted_units.why_material: Carries the block idea through weights, truncation errors, coefficient computation, and a critical evaluator assumption, giving a reusable reduction from the entire main sum to many normalized polynomial exponential sums.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the direct remainder series and explicit error allocation across blocks.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Several extracted arrays in equations (2.15)-(2.25) are visually noisy; structural claims are clear from surrounding prose.

accepted_units.title: Quadratic and cubic specializations yield exponents 1/3 and 4/13
accepted_units.why_material: Specializes the generic reduction and, for cubic blocks, splits at K=t^(1/13) so either direct lattice FFT or Theorem 2.2 has the same t^(4/13) precomputation scale.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes Theorem 2.3 and the final derivation of Theorem 1.1.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Exponent algebra and lattice dimensions depend on displayed formulas but are textually explained.

accepted_units.title: What must change to beat 4/13
accepted_units.why_material: Identifies lower cubic precomputation cost or control of larger cubic coefficients as the improvement lever, notes possible amortization, and separates the 1/3 method from reliance on Riemann-Siegel.
accepted_units.context_note: A concise source-authored boundary on the result's reach.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low; only exponents are typeset-dependent.

accepted_units.title: Quadratic van der Corput descent as the model mechanism
accepted_units.why_material: Connects Poisson summation to van der Corput stationary contributions, explains Gaussian self-similarity and coefficient normalization, and shows how repeated length halving plus inexpensive nonstationary remainders gives a polylogarithmic quadratic evaluator.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the role of incomplete Gamma functions in certifying remainders.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The precise transformation and remainder bound depend on equations (3.1)-(3.4).

accepted_units.title: Small cubic coefficient restores approximate self-similarity
accepted_units.why_material: Diagnoses the square-root phase created by cubic stationary points, then uses a small-coefficient expansion to absorb quartic and higher terms and recover a short linear combination of cubic sums with controlled error.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the explicit transformed coefficients and why the stronger stopping inequality is eventually needed.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-intensive; exact signs and constants require the typeset equations, while the obstruction and repair are clear in prose.

accepted_units.title: Iterate while self-similar, then route boundary cases
accepted_units.why_material: Separates inexpensive nonstationary remainders, small-length direct evaluation, Euler-Maclaurin handling when the quadratic coefficient is small, and a final precomputed high-degree sum when cubic self-similarity fails.
accepted_units.context_note: Ends with the complete source summary of the K^(4 mu) precomputation mechanism.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Coefficient recurrences and terminal length estimates depend on displayed formulas.

accepted_units.title: Reuse quadratic machinery through integral factorization
accepted_units.why_material: A prototypical cost count explains four parameter dimensions, then the author deliberately replaces a literal cubic iteration by a factorization that reuses an existing quadratic-sum algorithm.
accepted_units.context_note: Bridges the conceptual iteration to the actual implementation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low to moderate; parameter powers are formula-dependent.

accepted_units.title: Decouple, descend quadratically, extract saddles, then precompute
accepted_units.why_material: Gives the whole implemented pipeline: express a cubic sum as an integral of quadratic and cubic factors, weaken their coupling, apply quadratic descent, extract stationary contributions as constrained higher-degree sums, and evaluate them from an FFT grid.
accepted_units.context_note: The full span is needed because the precomputation claim depends on both earlier phases and the saddle-point output family.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Key integral identities and parameter bounds require checked displays (3.16)-(3.20).

accepted_units.title: Complexity conventions and easy coefficient regimes
accepted_units.why_material: Makes informal reductions precise in the paper's cost model and removes small K, negative mu, and moderately large cubic coefficients by direct evaluation, quadratic reduction, or lattice precomputation.
accepted_units.context_note: Provides the assumptions under which the detailed algorithm is subsequently valid.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Threshold inequalities and resource powers are formula-dependent.

accepted_units.title: Parity descent to the cubic-integral transition scale
accepted_units.why_material: Splits the Fourier integral into stationary and nonstationary x-regions, reduces the nonstationary pieces to quadratic sums, and repeatedly separates even and odd cubic terms until cN^2 reaches a controlled scale while the coupling coefficient remains small.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the terminal bounds (4.9), which are the contract for phase two.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-dependent, especially the S-functions, parity recurrence, and terminal inequalities.

accepted_units.title: Normalize coefficients while trading quadratic length for coupling growth
accepted_units.why_material: Applies periodic normalization and the quadratic transformation repeatedly; each step halves the quadratic length while amplifying the coupling parameter, with explicit invariants and three stopping conditions.
accepted_units.context_note: Ends at the definition of the exact stopping iteration.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Exact transformed coefficients and invariants in (4.10)-(4.16) require the displays.

accepted_units.title: Reduce every second-phase stopping route to controlled integrals
accepted_units.why_material: Handles short-length and small-quadratic-coefficient exits, decomposes inherited remainders into explicit function families, and uses interval localization, contour changes, and Taylor expansions to reach a single terminal double-integral interface.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the terminal parameter bounds needed by saddle-point extraction.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Several long formulas are OCR-sensitive; the case split and reduction logic are recoverable from prose.

accepted_units.title: Stationary contributions turn the terminal integral into a phase sum
accepted_units.why_material: Separates computable tails, extends the bulk contour, evaluates the Gaussian x-integral, centers at each y-stationary point, and reduces the result to one nonquadratic phase sum plus quadratic sums already handled by Theorem 2.1.
accepted_units.context_note: The full span is needed to see why contour errors and endpoint pieces are not hidden costs.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Highly formula-dependent; exact stationary points, series coefficients, and contour contributions require the typeset source.

accepted_units.title: Bounded analytic tail becomes a finite polynomial-phase family
accepted_units.why_material: Uses coefficient decay and the relation between N and M to truncate the stationary phase series at degree 3+floor(log N/log M), expanding the remaining bounded tail outside the exponent.
accepted_units.context_note: Produces exactly the sum family consumed by the FFT phase.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The degree and coefficient bounds in (4.41)-(4.43) are display-dependent.

accepted_units.title: Dyadic approximation and FFT grids for the large-M regime
accepted_units.why_material: Decomposes arbitrary lengths into powers of two, tracks how phase coefficients transform, discretizes them at derivative-controlled resolutions, and proves an FFT cost bounded by the desired fourth power when M is not too small relative to N.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the degree-at-most-12 consequence for this regime.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Dense formulas and product bounds require exact typeset verification.

accepted_units.title: Exploit coefficient dependence when the polynomial degree grows
accepted_units.why_material: Shows why treating higher coefficients independently is too costly for small M, reparameterizes all of them through six linked variables, derives analytic interpolation radii, and obtains a sparse FFT grid within the K^(4 mu) budget.
accepted_units.context_note: This is a distinct structural repair to the naive high-dimensional lattice, not routine cost bookkeeping.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The dependency formulas, Cauchy bounds, and discretization counts are formula-dependent.

accepted_units.title: Euler-Maclaurin decomposition with explicit remainder
accepted_units.why_material: Provides the discrete-to-integral conversion and remainder inequality used at algorithmic boundary points.
accepted_units.context_note: Lemma 5.1 is short but supplies the formal interface for later derivative control.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Exact Bernoulli correction indices and constants require the display.

accepted_units.title: Recursive derivative bounds make few Euler-Maclaurin corrections sufficient
accepted_units.why_material: Represents derivatives by recursively generated polynomials, controls their coefficient norm, and turns small cK^2 into logarithmically many accurate correction terms with bounded precision.
accepted_units.context_note: Captures both analytic error control and computational evaluability.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Recursion and norm bounds are formula-dependent but legible.

accepted_units.title: Euler-Maclaurin correction integrals reduce to quadratic sums
accepted_units.why_material: Splits terms according to whether a linear frequency is small, uses local Taylor expansion in the small region and explicit integration in the large region, and controls cancellation by shifting the summation index before binomial expansion.
accepted_units.context_note: This supplies the mechanism behind repeated claims that correction terms are efficient.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-dependent, particularly rational-weighted exponential sums (5.12)-(5.15).

accepted_units.title: Move nonstationary cubic contours into exponentially decaying directions
accepted_units.why_material: Uses Cauchy deformation and small cK^2 to create exponential decay, truncate long contours to logarithmic length, and reduce the resulting integrals to the quadratic-sum interface.
accepted_units.context_note: Lemma 5.4 certifies the nonstationary pieces discarded in phase one.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Contour definitions and decay exponents need the typeset formulas.

accepted_units.title: Partition by stationary geometry and reduce to Airy-type integrals
accepted_units.why_material: Handles a broad cubic-quadratic double integral by separating small and large quadratic curvature, then partitions y by stationary-point location, deforms contours for decay, and reduces all cases to controlled Airy variants and incomplete Gamma functions.
accepted_units.context_note: Represents the common evaluator invoked throughout the boundary and tail arguments.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Highly formula- and contour-dependent; prose safely supports the case architecture, while exact phases require scan-quality equations.

accepted_units.title: External contour tails collapse back to quadratic exponential sums
accepted_units.why_material: Proves that the extended x-contours used in saddle extraction are cheap by rotating the y-contour, exploiting uniform decay, separating a full Gaussian integral from a decaying half-line correction, and reducing both to quadratic sums.
accepted_units.context_note: Closes the last unverified cost path in the cubic algorithm.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Dense contour and Gaussian formulas are OCR-sensitive; exact constants and orientations require the typeset source.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Block scale as an algorithm-design dial
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Choosing block length jointly sets the global query count, local phase degree, coefficient ranges, and the precomputation dimension, so the final complexity exponent is a balance between representation compression and evaluator coverage.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: This balance is proved only for the source's zeta reduction and stated quadratic/cubic evaluators; it is not a general lower-bound principle.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Intervention makes repeated transformation progressive
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Poisson or van der Corput transformation shortens sums only because coefficient normalization and small-tail expansion intervene between steps to restore an approximately closed representation class.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Closure is conditional on the small cubic coefficient and explicit stopping inequalities.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Adaptive exits are part of the algorithm, not exceptions
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The algorithm gains efficiency by routing different failures to direct evaluation, Euler-Maclaurin, quadratic descent, saddle analysis, or precomputed lookup rather than forcing one recursion through every parameter regime.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The routing relies on source-specific inequalities and the prior quadratic evaluator.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Stationary analysis compresses analytic geometry into a finite query family
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Contour extension and saddle extraction isolate the oscillatory mass, after which coefficient decay converts an analytic phase into finitely many grid-addressable polynomial-phase sums.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The exact compression and degree bound depend on the terminal N/M parameter relation.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Respect dependencies before discretizing parameters
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: A naive independent grid becomes too large when the phase degree grows; exposing shared generating parameters among higher coefficients reduces the effective dimension enough to restore the target FFT budget.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The six-parameter relation comes from this particular stationary-phase expansion and does not assert universal low-dimensional structure.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Auxiliary lemmas form a cost-certification stack
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Derivative bounds certify short Euler-Maclaurin expansions, nonstationary contours certify decay, saddle-aware integrals reduce to Airy or incomplete-Gamma forms, and remaining terms return to the quadratic-sum interface.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: This synthesis establishes the paper's claimed computational reductions, not numerical practicality or optimized constants.
